scenarios.title: Two Stopping Fixtures
scenarios.answer: Same impulse; longer supplied stopping time lowers average-force magnitude.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: For the same momentum change, which duration lowers average-force magnitude?
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain what stays fixed, what changes, and the direction and limits of the model.
scenarios.keyIdea: Average net force = Δp / Δt. Keep the system boundary and signs explicit; this model does not predict injury.
hints: For the stated system, Δp = mass × (final velocity − initial velocity).
Divide signed Δp by each supplied duration. Compare magnitudes; longer duration changes force, not required Δp.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: 60(0−20) = −1200 kg·m/s. Dividing by 0.06 and 0.15 gives −20000 and −8000 N; same impulse, different average force.

scenarios.title: System Boundary Check
scenarios.answer: Use the occupant mass for the occupant ledger. Do not insert the whole vehicle mass.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Which mass belongs in the occupant momentum ledger?
predictions: Sum of vehicle and occupant masses
scenarios.explanationPrompt: The ledger is for the occupant. Explain why its mass is used rather than the whole vehicle mass.
scenarios.keyIdea: Name the system first. Occupant and vehicle masses belong to separate momentum ledgers.
hints: For the stated system, Δp = mass × (final velocity − initial velocity).
Divide signed Δp by each supplied duration. Compare magnitudes; longer duration changes force, not required Δp.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: The occupant system uses 60 kg. The 1200 kg vehicle belongs to a separate ledger and cannot substitute for occupant mass.

scenarios.title: Locking Carts
scenarios.answer: Combined momentum is conserved in the supplied low-friction system; kinetic energy is not claimed conserved.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Which momentum account applies when the supplied low-friction carts lock?
predictions: Kinetic energy must always be conserved
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Define the two-cart system, show its signed momentum before and after locking, and explain the external-impulse assumption and kinetic-energy limitation.
scenarios.keyIdea: With negligible external impulse, combined momentum is conserved. Kinetic energy is not claimed conserved in the locking collision.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: Initial momentum is 2×3 + 1×0 = 6 kg·m/s. Combined mass 3 kg gives +2 m/s after locking. External impulse is negligible; kinetic energy is not claimed conserved.
